title: C++ App, Brand Design Package
desc:
I need one skilled partner who can move comfortably between code and creative visuals. The first and most important task is a fully-functional C++ program. Once the software piece is underway and clearly scoped, I also want to establish a cohesive visual identity for my new venture: a clean, text-based logo, matching business card artwork, and a reusable YouTube thumbnail template.

Here’s how I picture the hand-off:

• C++ program – compact, well-commented, ready to compile on Windows; deliver source files plus a brief README that explains build steps and usage.  
• Logo – minimalist, text-only mark delivered in vector (AI / SVG) and web (PNG) formats, with colour and black-on-white versions.  
• Business card – print-ready PDF (3.5" × 2" plus bleed) and editable source file, using the new logo and consistent typography.  
• YouTube thumbnail – 1280 × 720 px layered PSD / AI template that matches the card and logo styling.

I’m aiming for an orderly, on-time rollout: finish the C++ build first, then move straight into the design items so everything ships together. If you can juggle both disciplines or coordinate seamlessly with a teammate, let’s talk about the specifics and get started right away.

title: Website Text Data Entry
desc:
The job is straightforward: extract text-based information from a series of specified websites and enter it accurately into a structured spreadsheet I will provide (Google Sheets or Excel, whichever you prefer). All content comes solely from online sources—no PDFs, scans, or handwritten material—so quick copy-and-paste accompanied by careful formatting will be the main workflow.  

Accuracy and consistency are critical; spelling, punctuation, and capitalization must match the source exactly. Please maintain the column order already set up in the template and avoid introducing extra spaces, line breaks, or styling. When a field on the page is empty, leave the corresponding cell blank rather than inserting placeholders.  

Deliverables  
• Completed spreadsheet containing all requested website text, fully checked for errors  
• Brief note outlining any sites that were unreachable or had missing sections so I can follow up  

The sheet currently has 1,200 rows allotted, and I expect the work to be finished within five days of acceptance. Feel free to use browser extensions or basic scraping tools if they speed up clean extraction, but the final output must remain human-readable and neatly formatted. Drop any clarification questions before starting so we stay perfectly aligned.

title: Therapeutic Inhalation Device Hardware Design
desc:
I need a complete electronic hardware solution for a therapeutic, drug-delivery device that administers medication via inhalation. The brief covers everything from early-stage architecture to a working, testable prototype.  

The hardware must precisely control dose release, monitor key parameters such as airflow and temperature, and log usage data for later analysis. Size, power consumption, and patient safety are critical. Expect the design to comply with IEC-60601 and ISO-13485 principles, ready for eventual regulatory submission.

To keep the project clear, here is what I expect to receive:  
• Detailed schematics and PCB layout files (Altium, KiCad, or similar)  
• Component-level bill of materials with sourcing information  
• Firmware source code to drive sensors, actuators, and user interface elements  
• Functional prototype assembled and proven on the bench, including basic test results  
• Brief verification plan outlining how the design meets inhalation drug-delivery requirements  

If you have a background in therapeutic or diagnostic electronics, especially inhalers, nebulizers, or similar devices, and can guide decisions around sensors, microcontrollers, power management, and safety isolation, I’d like to hear how you would tackle this.

While you work in Tally, keep an eye on the Excel trackers I provide for inventory, tax summaries and other management numbers, updating them so that my weekly MIS report can be produced without last-minute scrambling.  

Accuracy, consistency and on-time delivery matter more to me than sheer speed. If you already handle GST, reconciliation and data analysis inside Tally and Excel every day, this assignment should feel familiar. I am happy to answer procedural questions, but I rely on you to notice missing bills, wrong tax codes or mismatched balances before they become problems.  

Deliverables I will review and sign off each period:

• GST-ready invoices in the custom format you design  
• Reconciled bank, debtor and creditor ledgers with supporting notes on variances  
• Updated Excel sheets for inventory, GST input/output and other

desc:
I run two story-driven YouTube channels—one centred on chilling horror tales, the other on timeless mythological legends—and I’m looking for a budget-friendly 2D animator who can give these narratives a lifelike feel. The style must stay firmly on the realistic side: believable anatomy, nuanced facial acting, atmospheric lighting and camera moves that build tension or awe as each scene demands.  

Every script arrives with a voice track or, when I need help sourcing talent, a request for you to supply it; in either case your animation must be precisely lip-synced and timed to the narration. Episodes typically sit in the short-form range (around the 8- to 10-minute mark), and I’d like to begin with one test video before moving into steady, ongoing production.  

What I need from you:  
• A reel or sample work that proves you can handle realistic 2D character animation.  
• A sense of your workflow and turnaround time for an episode of this length.  
• Confirmation that you’re comfortable either syncing to a provided VO track or arranging professional voice-over when asked.  
• Your preferred software—Toon Boom, Adobe Animate, TVPaint or any equivalent—so I know how best to share assets.  

Deliverables per episode  
• Full-HD (1920×1080) finished video, 24–30 fps, ready for immediate upload.  
• All project/source files so I can request minor tweaks or create shorter cuts later.  
• Final audio mix fully aligned with the animation.
